input: Summarise the emails I received last week and tell me which ones need a reply.

output.goal: Explain that I can’t access the user’s inbox, and request the email contents/metadata so I can summarize last week’s emails and flag which need a reply.
output.blocked_reason: I don’t have access to your email account or the messages you received, so I can’t summarize them directly. If you paste the emails (or a list with subject, sender, date, and body) from last week—or upload screenshots/files with sensitive info removed—I can summarize each and tell you which likely need a reply. You can also tell me what counts as ‘needs a reply’ (e.g., any direct questions, requests with deadlines, client messages, invitations).
output.output_format: When you provide the emails: a table with columns (Date, From, Subject, 1–2 sentence summary, Needs reply? Y/N, Why, Suggested response draft/next step, Priority) plus a short bullet list of the highest-priority replies.

e2e.output:
I can’t see your inbox or the emails you received, so I can’t summarize “last week” until you share the messages.

If you paste (or upload) the emails from last week—either full text or just **From / Subject / Date + body** (you can redact sensitive info)—I’ll:

- give a **one–two line summary per email**
- group them by theme (work, personal, bills, etc.)
- flag **Needs reply** vs **No reply needed**, with a suggested reply outline

To proceed, please send either:

1) **A batch**: copy/paste the emails from last week (best), or  
2) **A list**: for each email, paste:
   - From:
   - Subject:
   - Date/time (and your time zone):
   - Body:

Also tell me your rules for “needs a reply” (e.g., only direct questions; include meeting invites; include FYI messages from your boss; deadlines matter, etc.).
